name: Oxygen Sensor
summary: The N52 E90 has four oxygen sensors: two pre-catalyst (upstream, one per bank) and two post-catalyst (downstream). Part numbers 11787558055 (bank 1 pre-cat), 11787558073 (bank 2 pre-cat), 11787545074 (bank 1 post-cat, 560 mm lead) and 11787545075 (bank 2 post-cat, 490 mm lead) are corroborated across multiple retailers, with 328i/328xi fitment on the pre-cat listings; none were VIN-decoded. Socket is 22 mm (7/8 in) and an offset or crowfoot 22 mm tool is needed because of heat shield and tight access. Torque has a mild conflict (50 Nm per a quoted TIS value and 37 ft-lb, about 50 Nm, in one DIY, vs 55 Nm from another poster); both torque sources are not E90-specific TIS documents. Step-by-step connector locations are only partially documented (bank 2 pre-cat shield with two E8 screws; bank 1 plug toward the rear under engine cover), so the guide can be built with those sections flagged.
variantDependencies: N52B30 verified for these part numbers by Turner/ECS; N51B30 SULEV: Genuine BMW post-cat 11787545074/5 list N51, but N51 pre-cat sensor part numbers were NOT confirmed.
xDrive (328xi): Turner E90 listing shows 328xi for the pre-cat sensors; no differences in sensor routing found.
Sensor part numbers 11787537984 (M3) and 11787558087 (335i only) must not be used on a 328i.
Early-style 'silver top' Bosch sensors are mentioned for N52B; later sensor revisions/supersessions not verified.
Post-cat leads differ in length by bank (560 mm bank 1, 490 mm bank 2): wrong-bank orders will not fit.

A z4-forum thread quotes a TIS value of 50 Nm for a lambda socket with arm style (Z4 chassis, not E90) and a different poster citing 55 Nm; the poster says a straight socket would need slightly more. steps.title: Confirm which sensor is bad
steps.instruction: Read stored codes with a scan tool and confirm bank and position (sensor 1 pre-cat vs sensor 2 post-cat) before buying parts; one bavmods page contradicts itself about sensor 1 vs 2.

steps.title: Let the exhaust cool; disconnect battery
steps.instruction: Work cold. Disconnect the battery per the bavmods procedure.
warnings: Hot exhaust causes burns; sensors can seize and round off if forced.

steps.title: Remove engine cover and access panels
steps.instruction: Take off the three-screw engine cover; for the bank 2 post-cat sensor the DIY also removes the cabin filter housing, HVAC cowl and ECU covers (8 mm). Pre-cat sensor wiring runs under the engine cover, so the cover must come off; post-cat sensors may not need it.

steps.title: Locate sensors
steps.instruction: Four sensors: bank 1 (cyl 1-3, front) and bank 2 (cyl 4-6) each have an upstream (before cat) and downstream (after cat) sensor. Bank 1 upstream sits at the top of the front manifold with its plug further back; bank 2 upstream is behind a stainless shield held by two E8 screws; the post-cat sensors are between the manifolds area.
steps.status: VERIFIED (count and bank layout); SINGLE_SOURCE (individual locations)

steps.title: Unplug the connector
steps.instruction: Press the retaining tab and separate the plug; pre-cat leads are in channels/clips under the engine cover; some connectors must be freed before turning the sensor.

steps.title: Free the shield if needed
steps.instruction: For bank 2 upstream, remove the strut-tower-to-firewall brace and the large heat shield, then the two E8 shield screws (magnetic), to give the tool access.

steps.title: Loosen the sensor
steps.instruction: Seat the 22 mm crowfoot or offset wrench squarely and turn counter-clockwise; stop and escalate to a stronger tool only if it will not move, to avoid rounding the hex.
warnings: A rusted sensor may need penetrating oil; one poster hammered a cut-down wrench (risky).

steps.title: Prepare and install new sensor
steps.instruction: Apply a thin line of anti-seize to the threads only (not the tip), hand-thread to flush, then torque to the value confirmed from BMW TIS.
warnings: Torque value CONFLICT; do not publish until resolved.

steps.title: Reconnect and secure wiring
steps.instruction: Plug in the connector, secure the lead away from the exhaust with ties/clips, refit shield and brackets.

steps.title: Reassemble, reconnect battery, clear codes
steps.instruction: Refit covers in reverse, reconnect battery, clear codes with scan tool, check for return of codes and rough idle.

safety: Exhaust components retain heat; allow to cool fully before work.
Disconnect the battery as the cited DIY does before touching sensor wiring.
Keep anti-seize off the sensor tip and out of the sensor's reference holes.
Do not use cheap flare-style sockets; they round the hex (z4-forum author).
Support the vehicle correctly if raising it (general practice, not source-derived).
